title: Collecting Beyond Vectors
goal: Turn an iterator of Results into a single Result containing a collection.

sections.text: In languages like Python or JavaScript, collecting items into a list is a fixed operation. In Rust, `.collect()` is generic and works for many target types.

sections.code:
let nums: Vec<i32> = (1..=3).collect();
let set: HashSet<i32> = (1..=3).collect();
sections.caption: The target type tells collect what to build.

sections.text: You can also specify the type using turbofish syntax `.collect::<Vec<_>>()`. This is useful when chaining methods without an explicit variable binding.

sections.caption: Collecting an iterator of Results stops at the first Err.

sections.text: When iterating over `Result` items, collecting into `Result<Vec<T>, E>` unwraps every `Ok` into the vector. If any item is `Err`, iteration stops early and that `Err` is returned.
Collecting into `HashMap` and `BTreeMap` is covered in the Collections deck.

explanation: Turn an iterator of Results into a single Result containing a collection.
